COMMONJUDGMENT

The petitioner in M.V.C.No.6930/2022 filed claim petition under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act,
seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The petitioner in M.V.C.No.6931/2022 filed claim petition under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
3. These two petitions have arisen out of the same accident.
Therefore as per the order on I.A.No.I, these two petitions have been clubbed together for common evidence and common disposal.
4. The case of the petitioners is as follows:-

That on 24-09-2022 at about 1-30 p.m., the petitioner in M.V.C. No.6930/2022 was riding Splender Plus motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-59-J-2044 along with pillion rider Mr.Mani B N who is the petitioner in MVC No.6931/2022.

When they reached Indlavdi cross,
at that time the driver of Tractor vehicle bearing Reg.no.KA-03-T-0490 came from opposite direction i.e from Jigani side towards Anekal in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle result of which petitioners in both the cases sustained injuries.

sentences.text: In order to prove the defence taken by the respondent no.2 they have examined the Branch Manager of ESI, Bommasandra as RW.1 and through him Ex.R1 and R2 are marked.

Ex.R1 is the letter addressed to the court by the Branch Manager ESIC,
Bommasandra to the effect that the said office has not made any kind of ESI cash benefit to the petitioner.
The Rw1 has produced even NIL ledger sheets.
The RW.1 has deposed that as per records they have not given ESI benefit to the petitioner.

18 . In the judgment relied by the learned counsel for respondent no.2, referring Sec.53 and 61 of the Employees State Insurance Act it was held that "the petition under the Workmen's Compensation Act or the Employees Compensation Act is barred and the victim has to approach the ESI Corporation for compensation.
In the said case, the victim had applied for ESI facilities and code was allotted to the victim.
The subscription to the ESI facility was categorically stated by respondent no.1 and 2 in their written statement.
The said fact was not denied by the petitioner.
However they contended that they have not availed the compensation under the ESI Act.
In the above referred case, the Hon'ble High  SCCH-24 10 MVC 6930/2022  c/w  6931/2022 Court has made reference of several judgment rendered by Hon'ble High Court and Supreme Court.
In all the cases specific observation was made with reference to the word "Employment Injury suffered by the victim .
It means Sec. 53 and 61 of ESI Act would apply only to the Employment Injury suffered by the victim during the course of employment.
19. In the present case, the petitioner has not suffered injury during the course of Employment.
It is nowhere the case that the petitioner has suffered injury during the course of employment.
The present petition is not filed under ECA.
Hence, the observation made in the aforesaid ruling has no application to the case in hand.

Hence, the claim petition filed by the petitioner is Mani vs Subramani on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51705796/
6 very well maintainable.

sentences.text: Hence additional issue in MVC No 6930/2022 is answered in the Negative.
20. Issue No.1 and 2 in M.V.C.NO.6930/2022 and M.V.C.No.6931/2022 :- As these issues are interconnected they are taken up together for common discussion to avoid repetition of facts.
SCCH-24 11 MVC 6930/2022  c/w  6931/2022  P.W.1- Chandra Kumar R is the petitioner in MVC 6930/2022 and P.W.2 - Mani is the petitioner in MVC No.6931/2022.

P.W.1 and Pw2 have given evidence to the effect that at the time of accident P.W.1 as rider and Pw.2 as pillion rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg No.KA-44-V-4114 were proceeding on Gowrenahalli village, Kasaba Hobli, Anekal Taluk, at that time, the driver of Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-03-T-0490 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came from opposite direction at very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's vehicle and caused the accident.

21 . In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 and PW.2 have relied upon Ex.P1 to P7 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, spot mahazar, seizure mahazar, wound certificate, IMV report, notice u/Sec.133 of IMV Act, statement of accused and charge sheet etc.,
 22.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by petitioner/Chandra Kumar in MVC No.6930/2022, case has been registered against the driver of offending  SCCH-24 12 MVC 6930/2022  c/w  6931/2022 vehicle in Crime No 0237/2022 of Anekal Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of MV Act.

The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279, 337, 338 of IPC.
 23.

The respondents No.2 has seriously disputed the manner of accident one stated by the petitioners and submitted that rash and negligent driving of the Mani vs Subramani on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51705796/
7 two wheeler by the Pw1 itself is the sole cause for accident.
Hence the liability to pay compensation may be fixed on the owner and insurer of the motorcycle.

24 . Though the petitioners in both the petition have categorically contended that the driver of the offending vehicle alone has contributed negligence and though the investigation officer after investigation has filed charge sheet only against the driver of the offending vehicle, but if the materials placed on record is perused, at the time of accident the petitioners were proceeding from Anekal towards Jigani and offending vehicle was coming from opposite direction i.e., from Jigani towards Anekal.

Though the PW.1 and PW.2 have  SCCH-24 13 MVC 6930/2022  c/w  6931/2022 deposed that the said road is one way road and the offending vehicle which came from wrong direction hit against their vehicle but if the spot mahazar is perused,
wherein it is mentioned that it is two way roads.
As it is a two way road there is provision to ply vehicles on both direction of the road.
The width of the as per Ex.P2 is 20 feet and the accident in question has occurred in the middle of the road.

When petitioners were proceeding from Anekal towards Jigani they ought to have ridden their vehicle on the left side of the road and when the driver of the offending vehicle was proceeding from Jigani towards Anekal he ought to have driven his vehicle on the left side of the said road.
But the PW.1 and the driver of offending vehicle by riding/driving their respective vehicle in the middle of the road have contributed equal amount of negligence.
It is relevant to state here that the petitioners have not produced eye sketch before the court.
It appears that intentionally the petitioners have suppressed the sketch before the court.

Hence, merely because the investigation officer has filed charge sheet only against the driver of the offending vehicle the court cannot on the basis of police document arrive at the conclusion that the driver of the offending vehicle alone is responsible for the accident.
As  SCCH-24 14 MVC 6930/2022  c/w  6931/2022 petitioner in MVC No.6930/2022 has contributed negligence to the extent of 50% he has to forgo compensation to the extent of 50%.

Further though petitioner in MVC No.6931/2022 is the pillion rider in Mani vs Subramani on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51705796/
8 the two wheeler but he has failed to array the owner and insurer of the motorcycle in which he was riding hence he is also to forgo compensation to the extent of 50%.

Even though the petitioner has stated that he has taken treatment as inpatient at General Hospital from 24-09-2022 to 30-09-2022 and was advised to come for regular follow up treatment up to 2 years, but no medical document to that effect is produced to show that petitioner has taken treatment at  SCCH-24 15 MVC 6930/2022  c/w  6931/2022 General Hospital, Anekal as inpatient.
